newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds drift, concerns over U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds drift, concerns over U.S. bonds.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat after a very slow session Thursday as concerns over the U.S. Treasuries market re-emerged following sharp gains earlier in the week.

"The local market was tranquil - there are some worries over the U.S. long-bond yield," said an analyst, pointing to a climb in the U.S. 30-year yield towards 7.0 percent Thursday. Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was unchanged at 93, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.03 at 122.83.

A trader suggested the market was returning to its slow mode before the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee this week as players began to worry that upcoming U.S. indicators could show a strong economy and lead the Federal Reserve to hike rates in coming months.
Traders said the market was not affected by the news from IBCA, the European rating agency, that it had assigned a BB rating to Argentine long foreign currency debt with a "positive" outlook.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.98 percent from 6.78 percent.
